access_audit_trail_enabled.title: Access Audit Trail Enabled
access_audit_trail_enabled.description: Attestation: an audit trail of access to customer/personal data is enabled and captured. Insecure (false) when no audit trail exists, leaving access events unrecorded.

at_rest_encryption_strength.title: At-Rest Encryption Strength
at_rest_encryption_strength.description: Strength category of the at-rest encryption applied to PII. 'none' means no encryption; 'weak' means deprecated algorithms / short keys / vendor-default keys with no rotation; 'strong' means modern AEAD (e.g. AES-256-GCM) with managed keys and rotation. Anything below 'strong' is treated as an exposure.

audit_log_tamper_evident.title: Audit Log Tamper Evident
audit_log_tamper_evident.description: Attestation: audit logs of PII access are tamper-evident — append-only / hash-chained / WORM storage — so post-hoc modification or deletion is detectable. Insecure (false) when logs can be silently altered, defeating breach attribution (NIST SP 800-53 AU-9).

audit_management_restricted_to_privilege.title: Audit Management Restricted To Privileged Subset
audit_management_restricted_to_privilege.description: Attestation: management of audit logs (rotation, deletion, configuration) is restricted to a privileged subset disjoint from the data-plane principals who act on the PII — separation of duties per NIST SP 800-53 AU-9. Insecure (false) when data-plane admins can also manage audit logs, enabling self-cover-up.

backups_encrypted.title: Backups Encrypted
backups_encrypted.description: Attestation that backups, snapshots, and exported datasets containing PII are encrypted. Backups are a frequent forgotten copy that re-exposes data even when the primary store is encrypted.

bulk_export_monitored_and_alerted.title: Bulk Export Monitored And Alerted
bulk_export_monitored_and_alerted.description: Attestation that volumetric / bulk-export anomaly monitoring is in place on the PII store with alerting on threshold breaches (row count, byte volume, query cardinality), so that mass-pull behaviour by an authenticated or compromised principal trips a signal. Secure value: true.

dlp_egress_controls_enabled.title: DLP Egress Controls Enabled
dlp_egress_controls_enabled.description: Attestation that DLP / egress-side controls are deployed and enforced on the PII data store's outbound paths (API, SQL, export), inspecting and blocking unauthorized bulk movement of customer/personal data. Secure value: true.

encrypted_at_rest.title: Encrypted At Rest
encrypted_at_rest.description: Attestation that the PII data store applies cryptographic encryption to data persisted on durable storage (database files, object storage, file shares). When false, anyone with media-level or volume-level access reads cleartext records.

field_level_protection_method.title: Field-Level Protection Method
field_level_protection_method.description: The field-level protection mechanism applied to sensitive fields at rest. Fires (insecure) when 'none' — no masking, hashing, tokenization, encryption, or pseudonymization is applied; record-level compromise exposes plaintext sensitive data.

governed_transfer_safeguards.title: Governed Transfer Safeguards
governed_transfer_safeguards.description: Attests that every cross-border transfer of PII to a non-adequate-decision country is governed by valid Article 46 GDPR safeguards — Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs), Binding Corporate Rules, or equivalent — accompanied by a documented Transfer Impact Assessment (Schrems II). False when any transfer lacks these safeguards.

hsts_enforced.title: HSTS Enforced
hsts_enforced.description: True when HSTS is enforced on browser-facing endpoints (Strict-Transport-Security with adequate max-age). False fires the exposure: a downgrade-back attack (sslstrip-style) can drop the client to HTTP and capture PII in cleartext.

key_rotation_enabled.title: Key Rotation Enabled
key_rotation_enabled.description: True when a rotation cadence is configured for the data-encryption keys (automatic KMS rotation, scheduled re-wrap, or operator-driven rotation with a defined interval). When false, a single key compromise persists indefinitely and the window for offline cryptanalysis is unbounded.

keys_derived_from_passphrase.title: Keys Derived From Passphrase
keys_derived_from_passphrase.description: True when the key-encryption key (KEK) or data-encryption key is derived from a human-chosen passphrase or low-entropy secret (e.g. a config-file password fed through PBKDF2/scrypt with weak parameters), rather than generated as full-entropy random material by an HSM/KMS. Low-entropy KEKs are tractable to offline brute-force once any wrapped blob leaks.

keys_managed_in_hsm_or_kms.title: Keys Managed In HSM Or KMS
keys_managed_in_hsm_or_kms.description: True when the data-encryption keys protecting this dataset are managed by a dedicated HSM or KMS (hardware-backed or cloud-managed key store) with access mediated by IAM/policy, rather than held as raw material alongside the application. When false, key material is held in plaintext config, environment variables, or the same storage tier as the ciphertext — defeating the encryption-at-rest control on any privileged read.

keys_stored_with_data.title: Keys Stored With Data
keys_stored_with_data.description: True when encryption keys are co-located with the ciphertext they protect — same database, same volume, same backup, or same blast radius. A single privileged read of the storage tier then yields both ciphertext and key, collapsing encryption-at-rest to no protection at all.

least_privilege_access_enforced.title: Least Privilege Access Enforced
least_privilege_access_enforced.description: True when access to the PII store is granted on a documented need-to-know basis, with role/service-account grants scoped to the minimum data each consumer requires (no broad blanket reads).

pan_rendered_unreadable.title: PAN Rendered Unreadable
pan_rendered_unreadable.description: Attests that Primary Account Numbers (PAN) and equivalent high-sensitivity identifiers are rendered unreadable anywhere they are stored (PCI DSS Req 3.5). Fires (insecure) when false — PAN stored in clear, directly usable on compromise.

pii_excluded_from_logs.title: PII Excluded From Logs
pii_excluded_from_logs.description: Attests that the application's logging, error-reporting, and tracing pipelines exclude raw PII / cardholder / health data from emitted log records, spans, and analytics events — preventing logs from becoming a shadow read of the primary data store (CWE-532).

relies_on_disk_encryption_only.title: Relies On Disk Encryption Only
relies_on_disk_encryption_only.description: Attestation that the only at-rest protection for PII is full-disk / volume-level encryption (e.g. LUKS, BitLocker, EBS volume encryption). Volume crypto protects against physical media theft but is transparent to a live OS — a compromised application, DB account, or host reads cleartext. Application/column/tablespace-level encryption is the recommended additional layer.

residency_confined_to_approved_regions.title: Residency Confined To Approved Regions
residency_confined_to_approved_regions.description: Attests that all PII storage locations (primary, backups, DR replicas, ad-hoc copies, caches, logs) are confined to the regions approved for the customer/contract/regulator (e.g., EU PII stays within EEA or adequacy-decision regions). False when any PII resides in or is processed from an unapproved region.

retention_schedule_enforced.title: Retention Schedule Enforced
retention_schedule_enforced.description: Whether a documented PII retention schedule is actively enforced across primary stores and backups (records purged at retention-end). When false, PII is retained indefinitely in violation of GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage-limitation and PCI DSS Req 3.2 retention discipline.

row_or_column_level_restriction.title: Row Or Column Level Restriction
row_or_column_level_restriction.description: True when row-level and/or column-level access controls scope each consumer to only the records and fields they need (e.g. tenant-scoped row filters, PII column masking) — not just table-level grants.

secrets_masked_in_logs.title: Secrets Masked In Logs
secrets_masked_in_logs.description: Attests that a masking/redaction pipeline is in place across log sinks (application logs, error reports, distributed-tracing spans, analytics events) that scrubs or tokenises sensitive fields before they are written or forwarded to centralised/archival systems.

secure_deletion_or_crypto_shred.title: Secure Deletion Or Crypto-Shred
secure_deletion_or_crypto_shred.description: Whether retention-end deletion applies NIST SP 800-88 Rev. 2 sanitization (Clear/Purge/Destroy) or crypto-shredding of PII across primary stores AND backups. When false, supposedly-deleted PII remains recoverable.

sensitive_fields_field_level_protected.title: Sensitive Fields Field-Level Protected
sensitive_fields_field_level_protected.description: Attests that high-sensitivity fields (card numbers, SSNs, government identifiers) are protected at the field level by at least one of: truncation, one-way hash, tokenization, field-level encryption, or pseudonymization. Fires (insecure) when false — sensitive fields stored in clear at record level, violating PCI DSS Req 3.3-3.5; database compromise yields directly usable credentials.

shared_admin_accounts.title: Shared Admin Accounts
shared_admin_accounts.description: True when administrative or service identities to the PII store are shared across people (no per-person attribution), so queries cannot be tied to an individual and a single credential compromise yields the whole dataset.

soft_delete_leaves_recoverable_pii.title: Soft Delete Leaves Recoverable PII
soft_delete_leaves_recoverable_pii.description: Whether the deletion pattern is a soft-delete (tombstone / flag) that leaves recoverable PII rows in the underlying store. When true, 'deleted' PII is still present and reachable to operators, queries, or backups.

storage_destinations_documented.title: Storage Destinations Documented
storage_destinations_documented.description: Attests that all PII storage destinations — including primary stores, backups, DR replicas, ad-hoc operational copies, and downstream processor locations — are inventoried and their geographic locations documented in the records of processing (GDPR Art. 30). False when storage destinations are unknown or undocumented.

tls_only_transport.title: TLS-Only Transport
tls_only_transport.description: True when PII is transmitted exclusively over TLS (no cleartext fallback / no plain HTTP listener). False fires the exposure: a cleartext channel is allowed, so a passive wire tap reads the data.

weak_tls_versions_enabled.title: Weak TLS Versions Enabled
weak_tls_versions_enabled.description: True when the transport accepts weak TLS versions (TLS 1.0/1.1) or weak ciphers, enabling an active MITM to negotiate a downgraded session and read the PII. Modeled as an interpreted boolean to avoid the regex/substring trap on composite cipher strings.
